method: A seeded random sample (seed 11) of 145 extracted rows from the census as it stood before the false-positive fixes was read by hand and judged: is this a string a person can be shown, worth translating? The model that wrote the extractor made these judgments, so they are not independent. An independent re-check of a fresh sample is in `data/INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md`.

tiers.tier: Syntax-derived (text between tags, expressions, accessible attributes)
Property-name heuristic (label, message, title, label maps)

notes: Misses found: text written for AI assistant tools, IANA time zone ids, SQL text, file names used as source references, and lowercase single-word props (name, kind, icon). Each class was fixed in the extractor after the audit.
Doubtful but counted correct: purpose tags such as `Tourist (base)` in starter checklist seed rows, which are probably shown but were not seen on a screen.
Precision after the fixes was not re-measured by the same judge.

Independent re-check (a separate session, seed 29, 16 rows per class, 80 rows): 74 of 80 correct, 92.5 percent. Text between tags 16 of 16, accessible attributes 16 of 16, candidate sentences 16 of 16, component props 14 of 16, property-name heuristic 12 of 16. The misses (icon and field names, starter checklist keys matched by code, a machine reason) were fixed afterwards; precision after the second round of fixes was not re-sampled.
